item.title: Echigo-Tsumari Art Field: Contemporary Art Across Rice Terraces — Guide
item.description: Echigo-Tsumari Art Field is the site of one of the world’s largest international art festivals (Triennale), held every three years since 2000, though a substantial number of installations remain permanently on display across a sprawling rural area covering roughly 760 square kilometres. Works by artists from dozens of countries are integrated into the landscape of terraced rice paddies, forests, abandoned schools and traditional farmhouses, creating an unusual art-viewing experience that doubles as an exploration of depopulating rural Japan and its efforts at revitalisation through contemporary art.

item.title: Toyama Glass Art Museum & Workshop: Contemporary Glass in a Kengo Kuma Building — Guide
item.description: The Toyama Glass Art Museum is housed within a striking building designed by renowned architect Kengo Kuma, part of the wider Toyama Kirari complex, and showcases contemporary glass art from Japanese and international artists across several gallery floors. Beyond the museum displays, visitors can also try a hands-on glassblowing workshop nearby, working under instructor guidance to shape molten glass into their own small piece to take home, reflecting Toyama’s modern reputation as a centre for contemporary glass art.

item.title: Aomori Museum of Art: Yoshitomo Nara's Aomori Dog — Guide
item.description: The Aomori Museum of Art is home to Yoshitomo Nara’s colossal 8.5-metre ‘Aomori Dog’, the white puppy that has become the prefecture’s modern icon. Jun Aoki’s half-buried white architecture echoes the archaeological trenches of the neighbouring Jomon site. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Aomori City, Aomori Hours ~9:30–17:00 (closed some Mon) Admission Around ¥510 (more for shows) Time needed 1–1.

item.title: Towada Art Center: Open-Air Contemporary Art — Guide
item.description: The Towada Art Center scatters world-class contemporary art across central Towada City. Its free outdoor sculpture park — with works by Ron Mueck, Yayoi Kusama and others — turns an ordinary street into an open-air gallery, while the compact indoor galleries hold striking permanent commissions. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Towada City, Aomori Hours ~9:00–17:00 (closed Mon) Admission Outdoor free; indoor ~¥1,800 Time needed 1–1.

item.title: Naoshima Art Island, Kagawa: The Complete Visitor's Guide
item.description: Naoshima is a small island of roughly 8 square kilometres in the Seto Inland Sea, about 50 minutes by ferry from Takamatsu. In the early 1990s, it was a quiet island with an ageing fishing population, a modest industrial presence, and no particular reason to appear on any travel itinerary. Over the following three decades, the Fukutake Foundation — the philanthropic arm of Benesse Holdings, based in Okayama — transformed it into one of the world’s most celebrated destinations for contemporary art and architecture.
